open_obligations: Note the two papers use 'process supervision' for different things.
Check Lightman et al.'s confounders: the PRM data was actively selected and smaller.
Note that Lightman et al. do not train the generator with RL, so competitiveness under RL is untested.
in.other_title: Process supervision has a negative alignment tax on math
in.rationale: Reppert et al. expect outcome-based training to eventually outcompete process supervision. Lightman et al. report process-supervised reward models beat outcome-supervised ones on MATH (best-of-1860: 78.2% vs 72.4%) and claim a negative alignment tax; 'process supervision' there means step-level reward labels, while Reppert et al. mean executing human-understandable decompositions.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether process-based supervision must lose to outcome-based training on performance, for reward models on MATH

text: The authors state that process supervision is currently ahead because LM capabilities are weak and complex tasks need multiple calls, but that without scalable infrastructure they expect outcome-based training to eventually crush process supervision performance-wise, leading to the alignment problems they describe.
title: Without infrastructure, outcome-based training may outcompete process supervision
